themes_detail.label: Dead trees surge in Park Slope
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints spiked to 7 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 1.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 522% increase (z-score: 5.58)—suggesting either a recent disease outbreak, storm damage, or neglect of street tree inventory in this heavily tree-lined neighborhood.
evidence: 7 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (522% spike, z-score 5.58)
Street tree health is a recurring community board budget priority (reconstruction/upgrade of parks and amenities)
1090 total snow/ice complaints over 90 days suggests winter stress on tree canopy may be compounding issue
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Department about tree disease or recent weather damage in CD306; request tree inventory health status
Talk to residents and block associations on Prospect Park West, Carroll Street, and other tree-lined blocks about visible decline
Investigate whether budget cuts to Parks maintenance or pruning programs have reduced preventative care

themes_detail.label: Green taxi complaints explode
themes_detail.summary: Green taxi complaints jumped to 3 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.2 per week—a 1100% spike (z-score: 6.35)—indicating a possible illegal or aggressive expansion of for-hire vehicle services in Park Slope, or a specific incident sparking complaints.
evidence: 3 green taxi complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks (1100% spike, z-score 6.35)
Spike is acute and recent—no pattern in prior data suggests this is a new problem, not chronic
Concurrent spike in illegal parking (39% up) and noise complaints may suggest coordinated unlicensed driver activity
reporting_angles: File FOIL request with TLC for green taxi license applications, violations, or complaints filed in or near CD306 in past month
Check 311 complaint text for locations and times of green taxi complaints to map if activity is concentrated
Interview residents on affected blocks and TLC enforcement unit about what prompted the complaints

themes_detail.label: Outdoor dining chaos escalates
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints tripled to 3 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.2 per week—a 1100% spike (z-score: 6.35)—potentially reflecting tension over Open Restaurants program expansion, rule violations, or noise/debris from dining sheds in residential areas.
evidence: 3 outdoor dining complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks (1100% spike, z-score 6.35)
Concurrent spike in commercial noise complaints (24 THIS WEEK vs. 10.6 average, +126%, z-score 3.55) likely driven by dining sheds
Park Slope's dense residential streets (e.g., Carroll Street, Prospect Park West) are incompatible with outdoor dining infrastructure
reporting_angles: Identify which restaurants have recently opened or expanded outdoor dining; check DOB permits against 311 complaints for geographic match
Interview residents on blocks with outdoor dining sheds about noise, rodents, and safety concerns
Obtain DCLA outdoor dining license database and cross-reference recent permits with 311 spike dates

themes_detail.label: Dangling street signs create hazard
themes_detail.summary: Street sign complaints spiked 433% with 4 complaints 3 weeks ago versus a baseline of 0.8 per week (z-score: 7.51)—indicating potential public safety risk from poorly maintained street furniture, though the spike occurred 3 weeks ago and should be verified for current status.
evidence: 4 dangling street sign complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.8 weekly baseline (433% spike, z-score 7.51)
Spike is dated (3 weeks old) and should be cross-checked against recent 311 data to confirm resolution or persistence
Street condition complaints (538 total over 90 days) suggest broader infrastructure maintenance gaps
reporting_angles: File 311 complaint data request for street sign complaints filed in past 2 weeks to verify if spike has persisted
Contact DOT about maintenance backlog for street signs in CD306 and request inspection schedule
Walk key commercial streets (Fifth Avenue, Seventh Avenue, Flatbush Avenue) to identify any visible hazards

themes_detail.label: Commercial maintenance emergencies spike
themes_detail.summary: Maintenance or facility complaints surged to 17 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 5.9 per week—a 189% increase (z-score: 4.17)—potentially signaling HVAC, plumbing, or electrical failures across multiple buildings, or concentrated issues at one or more facilities.
evidence: 17 maintenance/facility complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.9 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks (189% spike, z-score 4.17)
1206 DOB alteration permits filed in 90 days suggest active building work; spike may reflect construction-related failures or landlord neglect
Heat/hot water complaints remain elevated at 1,326 over 90 days; this week's spike may indicate seasonal HVAC failures
reporting_angles: Request 311 complaint text and addresses for this week's maintenance complaints to identify if one building or area is driving the spike
Cross-reference spike with DOB permit data to see if major renovations are creating collateral damage to utilities
Interview residents about specific facility outages (heating, water, electrical) and whether landlords are responsive
